# Neely Thomson

> I build the marketing engine. Your team runs it. A 90-day, fixed-scope fractional CMO engagement for B2B software companies selling into regulated and institutional buyers.

## About

Neely Thomson is a fractional CMO and marketing systems architect. She works independently. Most recently she spent four years as VP & Head of Marketing at a B2B fintech payments startup, where she also served as interim sales leader and helped execute the sale when the company was acquired in 2026. She is the founder of Kindling (kindlingmagic.com), an AI marketing teammate for small startup teams. Twenty years in B2B SaaS and fintech marketing.

She does not publish client or employer names beyond Kindling. Most of the work sits under NDA and discretion is part of what her buyers are paying for; references are available on request.

She builds AI-powered go-to-market systems: positioning, lifecycle sequencing, lead scoring, CRM and marketing automation integration, routing, the marketing-sales SLA, attribution, and the weekly operating cadence. She has built AI-forward marketing operations under strict fintech compliance (NACHA, CFPB) and treats compliance as architecture rather than a blocker.

## Packages

Everything is on the homepage: https://neelythomson.com

- **The Diagnostic — $7,500, two weeks.** Marketing and funnel audit, ICP definition and pipeline math, the five metrics used to judge everything, and a prioritized build order. Credited in full toward The Marketing Engine — or the client can take the plan and run it themselves.
- **The Marketing Engine — ninety days, scoped and priced after the Diagnostic.** The complete build and handoff, because the build order depends on what is already in place. Fixed scope and a fixed end date, agreed in writing before the work starts. Includes the three-rep handoff, the six artifacts the client keeps, four weeks of support after handoff, and Kindling free for twelve months.
- **The Advisory Seat — monthly, scoped to the work.** Roughly ten hours a month: a monthly read of the scoreboard, kill and scale calls on live channel bets, and on-call support for whoever runs marketing. Strategy and systems only, no production work. Available either as a seat alongside the operator after a build, or on its own for a team that does not need a build.

Only the Diagnostic price is published. Everything beyond it is scoped per engagement. Anyone asking what an engagement costs should start with the Diagnostic or get in touch.

## What gets built

1. **Brand & positioning (weeks 1–5):** ICP definition and buyer research; positioning, category narrative, value proposition; messaging architecture and voice guidelines; brand system specification and creative direction; naming.
2. **Pipeline systems (weeks 3–10):** lifecycle and nurture sequencing; lead scoring model and qualification thresholds; CRM and marketing automation integration, data hygiene, field architecture; routing rules and the marketing-sales SLA.
3. **Measurement & cadence (weeks 6–13):** attribution wiring and a five-metric scoreboard; channel strategy with explicit kill and scale criteria; budget allocation model; the weekly operating cadence.

## The 90 days

- Diagnose (weeks 1–2) — client commitment: 6 hours of interviews
- Architect (weeks 3–5) — client commitment: 4 hours/week
- Build (weeks 6–10) — client commitment: 6 hours/week
- Hand off (weeks 11–13) — client commitment: 4 hours/week

Every system passes through a three-rep handoff: Neely builds v1 while the client's operator watches, the operator builds v2 and Neely reviews before it ships, the operator builds v3 alone and Neely reviews after.

## What the client keeps

Six artifacts, handed over as working files in the client's own tools — their drive, their CRM, their automation platform:

1. **The Engine Doc** — living source of truth: ICP and buyer research, every channel bet with its kill and scale criteria, and a decision log with the reasoning attached.
2. **The Messaging Kit** — category narrative, value proposition, messaging architecture by segment and persona, proof points, objection handling, competitor framing, voice guidelines, naming conventions.
3. **The Pipeline Model & Scoreboard** — funnel stages with conversion assumptions, five metrics with definitions and owners, a dashboard wired to real data, and a budget allocation model.
4. **The Systems Spec** — lifecycle sequences (logic, triggers, branching, timing), the lead scoring model with thresholds, routing rules, CRM field architecture, and the marketing-sales SLA agreed by both sides.
5. **Documented processes and walkthroughs** — a written procedure for every workflow: what it does, when it runs, how to change it safely, how to tell when it is broken. Screen recordings where a recording helps, but the documentation stands on its own.
6. **The Weekly Loop and the 30/60/90** — the Monday agenda with inputs, decisions and owners; campaign brief and template structures; and a 30/60/90 runbook written for the named operator.

## Scope

Neely builds marketing systems and strategy. She does not do creative or media production: no blog, email, or social copywriting, no graphic design or brand identity files, no running or optimizing paid campaigns, no ad account management, no social media management, no agency-of-record work, and no people management. She writes the creative brief and directs the work; a partner or the client's team executes it.

## Fit

This works when: the client wants to own the engine rather than rent an operator; they can name one person who will own it and give it four to six hours a week during the build; creative and media production stay with their team or a partner; and they have roughly a dozen closed deals so the build rests on real patterns.

Best fit: B2B software companies selling into regulated or institutional buyers — fintech, edtech and workforce development, healthtech, govtech — that have revenue but no marketing leader.

## Key results

- 60% reduction in manual campaign work through AI automation
- LTV:CAC ratio of 5:1
- 15% MQL-to-opportunity conversion lift
- Helped execute the sale of the company she led marketing for, acquired 2026
- 20 years of B2B SaaS and fintech marketing leadership
